device.name: SQUAD Lab AD75019 crosspoint switch (qcdrivers Muxi)

facts.text: Muxi is a QCoDeS VisaInstrument that controls an AD75019 crosspoint switch over pyVISA
The constructor sets the baud rate (default 9600), newline write and CRLF read terminators and a 2000 ms VISA timeout, calls connect_message and clears the VISA handle
send_command queries the VISA handle; on VisaIOError it calls self.visa.handle.clear(), an attribute path the class never defines, before sleeping 0.1 s and querying again
switch32 returns 'Route skipped: disabled range' without sending a command for x or y in 12-15 or 28-31, and otherwise sends SWITCH32 x,y
status sends MUX:STATUS? PIN,OUT, a command the firmware does not register
reset sends *RST through send_command, which reads one reply line
printconfig sends PRINT and then reads a further line from the VISA handle
close closes the VISA handle
The firmware registers the commands *IDN?, *RST, STAT?, SWITCH16, SWITCH32, CLEAR and PRINT
*IDN? prints the line 'SQUAD, Arduino AD75019 Switch, 1.0, 1.0'
The *RST handler runs Clear, flushes the 16x16 and the 32x32 matrices and then prints 'Reset complete'
Clear sets both route buffers to zero and prints 'Clear complete'
SWITCH32 prints 'Route skipped: disabled range' for x or y in 12-15 or 28-31; otherwise it adds the route, flushes the 32x32 matrix and prints 'Route added 32x32'
STAT? x,y prints '16x16: ' and '32x32: ' each followed by 1 or 0 from isRouted of the two route buffers, or 'Usage: STAT? x,y' without two parameters
The two matrix objects share one PCLK, SCLK and SIN pin set
AD75019_24.flush shifts the route buffer out bit by bit and then pulses PCLK; clear sets every word of the buffer to 0
isRouted reads the bit of the configuration buffer, not the chip
The 32x32 matrix class's X and Y pin mappings have 32 entries
The 16x16 matrix class's X and Y pin mappings have 16 entries
The 16x16 matrix class's isRouted indexes its X and Y pin mappings with the x and y it is given
STAT? passes the x and y it parses to isRouted of both the 16x16 and the 32x32 matrix
Four AD75019 chips are daisy-chained for the 24x24 array, each with X12-X15 and Y12-Y15 disabled and grounded

operator_required.reason: the usable AD75019 X (input) pins depend on the crate wiring: the firmware's 32x32 buffer takes pins 0-31 (AD75019_24.h:115-116) and refuses 12-15 and 28-31 (firmware.ino:76-80), and the mux README says those pins are grounded (src/qcdrivers/squad/mux/README.md:9); which of the rest are cabled is deployment data

safe_state.description: every crosspoint open in the firmware's route buffers and shifted out to the chips: *RST clears both buffers, flushes them and prints 'Reset complete' (firmware.ino:51-56); the e-stop succeeds only when the next two lines, after every line still owed by an earlier command, are 'Clear complete' then 'Reset complete'; the analog switches are not sensed
